caption: Matrix Distributors, Inc. v. National Association of Boards of Pharmacy
citation_line: Matrix Distributors, Inc. v. National Association of Boards of Pharmacy, No. 2:18-cv-17462, ECF No. 184 (D.N.J. Dec. 4, 2020), aff’d in part, rev’d in part, No. 20-3638 (3d Cir. May 19, 2022)
headnote_district_ruling: Judge McNulty dismissed claims by pharmaceutical wholesalers challenging accreditation decisions by the National Association of Boards of Pharmacy and related actions by OptumRx.
qualification_rationale: The case addresses when a nationwide private accreditor can be treated as a state actor and whether New Jersey common law can impose due-process-like duties on powerful private standard setters.
appellate_posture_note: The Third Circuit affirmed dismissal of the § 1983/state-action and most remaining claims, but reversed in part in a precedential opinion because the complaint plausibly alleged a New Jersey common-law due process claim against NABP.
